title: Revelation 14:14–20
context: One like a son of man sits on a white cloud with a sickle, and the earth is harvested. Another angel gathers the grapes of the earth into the great winepress of God’s wrath, and blood flows from the press for a great distance.

verses.text: I looked, and saw a white cloud, and on the cloud one sitting like a son of man, having on his head a golden crown, and in his hand a sharp sickle.
verses.arminianNotes: One like a son of man on a cloud is most likely Christ (Daniel 7:13).
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Christ as the one who brings the harvest.

verses.text: Another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to him who sat on the cloud, “Send your sickle and reap, for the hour to reap has come; for the harvest of the earth is ripe!”
verses.arminianNotes: An angel calls for the harvest because it is ripe.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s appointed time.

verses.text: He who sat on the cloud thrust his sickle on the earth, and the earth was reaped.
verses.arminianNotes: The earth is harvested. Some see the gathering of the righteous, others judgment.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note both readings, with many seeing the gathering of God’s people.

verses.text: Another angel came out of the temple which is in heaven. He also had a sharp sickle.
verses.arminianNotes: Another angel has a sharp sickle.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see preparation for judgment.

verses.text: Another angel came out from the altar, he who has power over fire, and he called with a great voice to him who had the sharp sickle, saying, “Send your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, for the earth’s grapes are fully ripe!”
verses.arminianNotes: An angel with power over fire calls for the grape harvest.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers link the fire to the altar and the prayers of the saints.

verses.text: The angel thrust his sickle into the earth, and gathered the vintage of the earth and threw it into the great wine press of the wrath of God.
verses.arminianNotes: The grapes are thrown into the winepress of God’s wrath, recalling Isaiah 63 and Joel 3.

verses.text: The wine press was trodden outside of the city, and blood came out of the wine press, up to the bridles of the horses, as far as one thousand six hundred stadia.
verses.arminianNotes: Blood flows up to horses’ bridles for 1,600 stadia. Most read the number symbolically, as a judgment covering the whole land.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the completeness of judgment.
